issues.detail: The Greek 'το θειον' (the divine/that which is divine) is the subject of the verb 'ειναι' (is). The Vietnamese translation 'bản thể thiêng liêng' (divine essence/substance) adds a philosophical concept ('essence') not present in the Greek text. Furthermore, the Vietnamese structure suggests the 'divine' is being compared to gold/silver/stone as 'objects of craft', whereas the Greek says 'the divine IS like gold/silver/stone [in terms of] craft and memory of man'.
